questions.title: Trim T003 to the confirmed test scope, or widen validate_state scope with an unparsable baseline `at`?

options.A: Keep the confirmed scope, trim T003: drop the unparsable-`at` and write_run checks; plan Q1 confirmation stays current.
options.B: Accept the widened scope: add 'unparsable `at`' to validate_state; fresh acceptance of all seven seams and failure paths.

questions.title: How does the orchestrator tell apart implement-gate refusal causes?

options.A: Read run state, not reason text: after a refusal read `factory show`; open pending_clarify or unanswered requires_user question routes to clarify or the relay wait with no cycle charged; no stored analyze.baseline (analyze-record always stores a derivable one first) asks fresh baseline/override/abort; otherwise unmet targets run a cycle when loops < 2, else the exhaustion question.
options.B: Stable cause tags in the refusal (protected:, baseline:, targets:).

questions.title: Keep the first report file when a lite run escalates and analysis runs again?

options.A: Stored counts are authoritative; reuse the pass number.
options.B: Keep the first report file: the orchestrator names the escalated re-analysis `factory/analyze-<n>-full.md`; prose-only change in SKILL.md and spec-builder.md, pass and loops untouched.

questions.title: How is 'implementation waits while remediation questions are pending' enforced with no writer for analyze.pending_clarify?

options.A: Routing enforces, gate check is defensive: relay routing (remediate envelope -> clarify) enforces FR-007's pending_clarify clause; the gate check fires only when state carries the field; no new writer.
options.B: Persist pending_clarify via checkpoint remediate --envelope (widens scope).

questions.title: Zero reports: what does the gate say and the orchestrator do?

options.A: Keep the existing 'analyze.reports is empty' refusal; the orchestrator runs analyze with no user question; FR-011 and US2 scenario 6 cover one or more reports only.
options.B: Treat as untrustworthy baseline and ask.
